answer.answer: No. The dSph gamma-ray limit uses the one-sided 95% threshold: 2[ln L_max − ln L(<σv>_95)] = 2.71 (TS drop of 2.71, i.e. a log-likelihood drop of 1.355). It profiles over the J-factor normalization of each dwarf (J = sJ0, Gaussian penalty on log10 s with width σ_J from the stellar-kinematic J uncertainty, profiled over log10 s in [-3,3]). The AMS-02 antiproton limit instead uses ΔQ = Δ(-2 ln L) = 3.84, the nominal two-sided 95% interval threshold for one parameter of interest, taking its upper endpoint. The paper says this differs from the usual one-sided 2.71 prescription. It profiles over the diffusive-halo half-height L (Gaussian penalty in log10 L, with L̂ = 4.96 kpc and σ = 0.197, profiled over 1 ≤ L/kpc ≤ 12).
